caption: Average Change in INC score from combined layer to base layer, where a negative score means the base layer was better than the combined one and vice versa. The gray and orange bars indicate whether the input to the compression layer is inferred frames or lexical signal, respectively. In all cases, inferred frames has a better effect on base layer and lexical signal has improved combined layer's performance.
model_annotation: This grouped bar chart illustrates the average change using compression across various observation probability categories for two different input types. The horizontal axis contains the categories, labeled "Observation Probability," which are displayed as discrete values of 0.2, 0.4, 0.5, 0.7, and 0.9 in ascending numerical order. The vertical axis represents the continuous value, labeled "Average Change Using Compression," using a linear scale that ranges from -3 to 2 with tick labels at regular intervals of 1. A prominent horizontal baseline at the zero mark visually separates positive and negative values. For each observation probability, there is a pair of side-by-side grouped bars; according to the legend at the bottom, the gray bar on the left of each pair represents "Inferred Frames," and the light orange bar on the right represents "Lexical Signal." All gray bars extend downwards, indicating negative values that span from the lowest point at approximately -2.9 for the 0.2 category to roughly -1.2 for the 0.9 category. Conversely, the light orange bars primarily extend upwards into positive values, with the exception of the 0.2 category, which displays a marginal negative value of roughly -0.1. The tallest positive light orange bar occurs at the 0.5 category with an approximate value of 2.1, while the 0.4, 0.7, and 0.9 categories show positive values of roughly 0.9, 1.4, and 1.5, respectively. The chart includes a light background grid composed of horizontal and vertical lines, and the groups are arranged sequentially without any individual bars being distinctly highlighted, outlined, or annotated.
